source.title: Memorization Sinks: Isolating Memorization during LLM Training
source.authors: G. R. Ghosal; Pratyush Maini; Aditi Raghunathan

record.tranche_reason: Tests memorization and generalization tradeoffs during language-model pretraining, extending the subject to repeated natural-text sequences in LLMs; it does not test the listed versions' settings or measures.
record.gate_note: Reports results on post-hoc localization, gradient-masked training, and MemSinks. These concern LLM memorization and validation performance, not the classification settings or specific measures defined by V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures verbatim memorization of repeated text, neuron-removal costs, and a proposed language-model training method. It does not test any V1–V8 comparison. Natural-text memorization is not V1's random-label fitting; removing neurons or deduplicating repeated documents is not V8's removal of high-influence examples versus equally many random examples. Sequence-dependent masking is not a test of V6's classifier dropout claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that standard training can entangle natural-text memorization with general capabilities, making post-hoc removal costly. They present MemSinks as a proof of concept for partly isolating memorization while preserving validation performance, with limitations involving small controlled experiments, sequence-ID metadata, larger-scale capabilities, and untested adversarial extraction.
record.recipe_differences: Autoregressive language-model pretraining on repeated TinyStories or SlimPajama data, followed by neuron localization or removal; not the supervised classification protocols in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with sequence type (natural text versus canaries), activation ratio, model size, sequence-ID noise, and whether memorization neurons are removed during evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural repeated text is harder to remove through neuron localization without validation degradation than atypical canaries; repeated-sequence and validation losses decline together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization of natural repeated text can share mechanisms with language-model generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient routing worsens validation loss, and removing designated memorization neurons further harms validation performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Routing repeated-example gradients to separate neurons does not ensure generalization-preserving unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: MemSinks reduces repeated-sequence memorization while preserving validation performance in tested settings; effectiveness depends on activation fraction, model size, and sequence-ID consistency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequence-dependent neuron masking can partly isolate verbatim memorization from language-model validation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: MemSinks exhibits smaller learning–forgetting fluctuations and lower later training loss on a repeated sequence when its assigned sinks are active.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequence-dependent sink neurons can protect repeated-sequence memorization from interference during training.

record.problems: Most experiments are small-scale and controlled; the authors identify limited investigation of large-scale capability effects and dependence on duplicated-example sequence-ID metadata. Many numerical outcomes are presented only in figures, and the text gives qualitative comparisons rather than uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels using the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, including locality and initialization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions and recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out classifier error, including small datasets, excessive dropout, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing high-influence memorized examples versus equally many random examples and comparing test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not identify a listed effect; this does not dispute the reported off-claim findings. Method comparisons and hyperparameter selections may be retained as context but should not serve as evidence for these versions. No additional result in the supplied text warrants a version-linked missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test accuracy on natural versus random labels; the stated architectures and training recipes.
Width sweep past interpolation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the stated connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on image-classification or language benchmarks under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and the listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in the stated classifier settings, including the small-training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures of the training–test gap.
Removing high-influence memorized examples versus random examples and measuring test accuracy on the stated datasets.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Pruning identified neurons and measuring sequence forgetting and validation-loss degradation.
rows.measure: Tradeoff between repeated-sequence loss increase and validation-loss degradation.
rows.value: Dropping identified neurons increases memorized-sequence loss; the method struggles to remove typical sequences.
rows.note: Authors characterize localization methods as achieving only partial success; numerical values are presented in the figure.
rows.check: Post-hoc neuron pruning measures unlearning and validation degradation, not any listed version. The qualitative result is consistent with the text.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Integrated Gradients localization followed by neuron dropout.
rows.measure: Repeated-sequence loss increase and validation-loss degradation.
rows.value: Less effective at removing memorization than in TS-Canary; generally produces less model degradation than pruning.
rows.note: The text gives the direction of results, not numerical values.
rows.check: Integrated Gradients localization measures unlearning, not a listed effect. The qualitative comparison is supported.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Pruning and Integrated Gradients localization followed by neuron dropout.
rows.measure: Repeated-sequence loss increase and validation-loss degradation.
rows.value: Integrated Gradients is highly effective at removing memorization; post-hoc removal causes less model degradation than in TS-Repetition.
rows.note: The text states the comparison qualitatively; figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Combines two methods with different outcomes: pruning has only partial success on canaries; Integrated Gradients is highly effective. Split by method if retaining these off-claim results.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Tracked validation and repeated-sequence losses during training.
rows.measure: Validation loss and repeated-sequence loss over training.
rows.note: This is a training-trajectory observation, not a test-error measurement.
rows.check: Simultaneous decreases in natural-sequence and validation losses do not measure random-label fitting or the natural-versus-random-label comparison required by V1.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-masked training, with repeated-example gradients routed to memorization neurons and other-example gradients to generalization neurons.
rows.measure: Validation loss relative to standard training with repeated data.
rows.value: Significantly worse validation loss, even before memorization neurons are removed.
rows.note: The paper describes the result as significantly worse but gives no numeric value in the text.
rows.check: Performance of a proposed gradient-routing intervention is not a test of V1–V8. Worse validation loss does not establish a reversal of any listed version.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium like architecture
rows.operation_detail: Removed memorization neurons after gradient-masked training.
rows.measure: Change in validation loss as training progresses.
rows.value: Validation loss becomes sensitive to removal of memorization neurons as training progresses.
rows.note: The text reports degradation but provides no numerical value.
rows.check: Removal of designated neurons after gradient routing measures co-adaptation, not removal of memorized training examples as in V8.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss with standard training, with and without repeated documents.
rows.value: Comparable validation loss; standard training with repeated sequences outperforms filtering repeated sequences out.
rows.note: The text states qualitative comparisons; precise values are figure-only.
rows.check: Combines MemSinks performance with a repeated-data versus deduplicated-data comparison. Neither comparison selects high-influence examples and compares their removal with random removal.

rows.subject: GPT Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Dropped memorization neurons and measured loss on repeated TinyStories documents.
rows.baseline: Standard trained model memorizes these sequences, achieving close to 0 loss.
rows.value: Loss increases to roughly 66% of a standard trained model that does not memorize.
rows.note: The stated comparison concerns repeated-sequence loss, not held-out test error.
rows.check: Repeated-document loss after removing sink neurons measures the proposed method's memorization mitigation. The text inconsistently calls p a dropout ratio and an activation fraction; Section 5.3 defines it as the activated fraction.

rows.subject: 360M SmolLM-style model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MemSinks and evaluated after removing memorization components.
rows.measure: Validation loss and memorization loss; validation–training loss gap.
rows.baseline: Standard training with and without repeated TinyStories data
rows.value: MemSinks validation loss outperforms the deduplication baseline and is comparable to the repeated-data baseline; memorization is mitigated, closing the validation–training loss gap by at least 50%.
rows.note: The paper gives the gap reduction as at least 50%; other comparisons are qualitative.
rows.check: Combines validation performance and memorization mitigation of the proposed method. Neither measure tests a listed version; the gap concerns repeated training examples, not an aggregate training-set loss.

rows.subject: 1.7B SmolLM-style model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MemSinks and evaluated after removing memorization components.
rows.measure: Validation loss and memorization loss; validation–training loss gap.
rows.baseline: Standard training with and without repeated TinyStories data
rows.value: MemSinks mitigates memorization without harming validation loss, outperforming or matching deduplicated training; memorization gap is closed by at least 50%.
rows.note: The text reports these outcomes across both large-scale settings; no numerical loss values are stated.
rows.check: Combines validation performance and memorization mitigation of the proposed method. The text reports at least 50% gap closure collectively across larger-scale experiments, without separate numerical estimates for each model.

rows.subject: GPT Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the fraction of memorization neurons activated per sequence.
rows.measure: Memorization isolation, measured by loss on repeated sequences.
rows.note: The text reports the preferred tested setting qualitatively.
rows.check: The best tested activation ratio is a hyperparameter-selection result for MemSinks, not an independent result on V1–V8.

rows.subject: GPT Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the fraction of memorization neurons activated per sequence.
rows.measure: Memorization isolation, measured by loss on repeated sequences.
rows.baseline: Lower activation ratios; p = 0.3 performs best.
rows.value: Performance breaks down at higher values, including p = 0.7.
rows.note: The authors hypothesize insufficient shielding from forgetting as the cause.
rows.check: An ablation showing failure of memorization isolation at p = 0.7 does not establish the opposite of any listed claim.

rows.subject: MemSinks models across tested sizes

conditions.value: normally trained model of same size

rows.measure: Repeated-sequence loss and validation-loss increase relative to standard training.
rows.baseline: Standard trained model of the same size
rows.value: Memorization is isolated across model scales, but validation-loss degradation grows as model architecture becomes smaller.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the size effect without giving per-size numerical values.
rows.check: A model-size ablation of MemSinks does not sweep width beyond zero training error as V2 requires.

rows.subject: MemSinks models
rows.operation_detail: Introduced inconsistent sequence IDs by randomly perturbing repeated-sequence IDs.
rows.value: Robust to small amounts of noise, up to 10%.
rows.note: No numerical loss value is stated.
rows.check: Sequence-ID noise robustness measures the proposed method's performance, not a listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: MemSinks models
rows.operation_detail: Introduced inconsistent sequence IDs by randomly perturbing repeated-sequence IDs.
rows.value: Fails to isolate memorization as effectively; consistent sequence IDs across repetitions are important to success.
rows.note: No numerical loss value is stated.
rows.check: Reduced memorization isolation under inconsistent sequence IDs measures a method limitation, not a listed claim.

rows.subject: GPT Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training loss on one repeated sequence over training for standard training and MemSinks.

conditions.value: single sequence observed every 40 gradient steps

rows.measure: Training loss fluctuations on the repeated sequence.
rows.value: MemSinks experiences lower-amplitude learning–forgetting cycles and maintains a lower training loss later in training.
rows.note: The figure is described qualitatively in the text.
rows.check: Repeated-sequence learning–forgetting dynamics do not measure any listed version. Unlike removal evaluations, this training-loss measurement includes the assigned sink neurons.
